decisions: Railpack is invoked as `<binary> build <workspace> --name localhost/easy-host-<app>:<UTC stamp> --progress plain`, with BUILDKIT_HOST injected into the child environment only; this uses the spike-corrected --name flag.

unsupported-source and build-failure use BuildError exit 3 with distinct stable codes (BUILD_UNSUPPORTED_SOURCE, BUILD_PROVIDER_FAILED); infrastructure-failure uses PrerequisiteError exit 2 with BUILD_INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILED and reason-specific remediation.

Streaming uses an ordered merged output queue and per-stream line splitters; each complete line is written immediately, unterminated lines are capped at 64 KiB, and only a bounded 20-line / 8k-character tail is retained for diagnostics.
App names are validated with validateAppName() and timestamps with a strict yyyymmddThhmmssZ formatter before entering the tag; the child is started with an argument array, never a shell.
A host-wide <stateRoot>/build.lock is acquired when stateRoot is supplied; the lifecycle caller must pass it to enforce the v1 one-build-at-a-time contract.
The default runner is a shell-free spawn seam so the shared platform runner can replace it; URL credentials and ANSI escapes are redacted by default.
A stalled image export is classified as docker-loader-unavailable with podman-docker remediation, reflecting the Phase 0 spike's docker-loader finding.

payload.taskDescription: Implement build.ts. Invoke the pinned Railpack binary with BUILDKIT_HOST pointed at the managed socket, the workspace as the build context, and an image tag of localhost/easy-host-<app>:<UTC timestamp>. Stream stdout and stderr line by line to stderr. Return the image reference on success. Classify failures into unsupported-source, build-failure, and infrastructure-failure, each with its exit code and remediation. Tests use a fake child process to cover success, no-provider detection, provider failure, socket unreachable, registry pull failure, and output streaming order.
